reconstructed_theorem: Let Gamma be a finitely generated torsion-free abelian group and let q_1,...,q_K be nonzero finitely supported Q-valued functions on Gamma. There is a homomorphism ell:Gamma->Z injective on the finite union U of their supports. For each row q_j=sum_{a in A_j} c_(j,a)[a], its moment sequence m_(j,k)=sum_a c_(j,a)ell(a)^k has infinite Hankel rank |A_j|. The leading |A_j| square Hankel determinant is the product of the nonzero weights and the squared Vandermonde product of the distinct projected atoms; moments through order 2|A_j|-1 reconstruct the projected atoms and weights.
independent_proof: Because Gamma is finitely generated and torsion-free, choose coordinates Gamma isomorphic to Z^d. Let U be the finite union of supports. For every distinct x,y in U, x-y is a nonzero integer vector. The product p(v)=product_(x!=y representatives) v dot (x-y) is a nonzero polynomial over Q. A nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on all Z^d, so choose v in Z^d with p(v) nonzero and define ell(x)=v dot x. This is a homomorphism on all of Gamma and is injective on U. For d=0, U has at most one point and the zero homomorphism suffices.

For one row, enumerate the distinct projected atoms alpha_1,...,alpha_r and nonzero rational weights c_1,...,c_r. With V_(u,i)=alpha_i^u for 0<=u<r and C=diag(c_i), the leading Hankel block is H_r=VCV^T.

The Vandermonde determinant is product_(i<j)(alpha_j-alpha_i). Therefore det(H_r)=product_i c_i times product_(i<j)(alpha_j-alpha_i)^2, which is nonzero. Arbitrary negative coefficients only change the sign through product_i c_i; C remains invertible.
Every finite Hankel block factors through the r atom columns, so its rank is at most r. Since H_r is nonsingular, the infinite Hankel rank is exactly r, not merely at least r.

Writing A(T)=product_i(T-alpha_i)=T^r+a_(r-1)T^(r-1)+...+a_0 gives sum_(j=0)^r a_j m_(k+j)=0. The equations k=0,...,r-1 use moments only through 2r-1 and have coefficient matrix H_r, hence determine a_0,...,a_(r-1). Factoring A recovers the projected atoms, and the first r moments solve the nonsingular Vandermonde system for the weights.

required_repairs.repair: Choose coordinates on Gamma itself, Gamma isomorphic to Z^d, and avoid the finitely many difference hyperplanes there. Equivalently extend rationally and clear denominators. The theorem is unchanged.

required_repairs.issue: The phrase 'signed rational functions on a group' neither states finite support nor unambiguously means Q-valued functions; as conventionally read, rational functions may have no finite support union.
required_repairs.repair: Replace it by 'nonzero finitely supported Q-valued functions on Gamma' or 'nonzero elements of Q[Gamma]'.
